name: Cantonese — Jyutping
notes: Jyutping (the Linguistic Society of Hong Kong Cantonese Romanization Scheme, LSHK 1993), the officially promoted romanization for Standard Cantonese. INITIALS: 19 onset letters/digraphs, each a single unit under AGENTS.md §2 test 2 (the labialized stops ⟨gw kw⟩ spell one segment /kʷ kʷʰ/, not a cluster: k+w already gives /kw/, so the aspiration and rounding riding on one onset earns the digraph its key) or test 3 (⟨ng⟩ /ŋ/ blocks a wrong n+g maximal-munch read; without the key ⟨ngo⟩ 'I/hungry' would tokenize n+g+o). FINALS: Jyutping's finals table is a designed syllabary of nucleus(+coda) units, exactly the precedent already accepted in this dataset for pinyin finals (⟨iang⟩, ⟨uai⟩) — every vowel-length distinction (⟨aa⟩ /aː/ vs ⟨a⟩ /ɐ/) and diphthong (⟨aai⟩, ⟨eoi⟩, ⟨oet⟩) is cited to its own IPA cell in the source table rather than derived by concatenating letters, since e.g. ⟨eoi⟩ /ɵy̯/ is not e+o+i by any compositional reading. CODAS: stop codas ⟨p t k⟩ are unreleased [p̚ t̚ k̚] in Cantonese finals (Matthews & Yip 1994), cited directly on the final rather than expressed as a `positional_graphemes` word-final rule, because in Jyutping — unlike POJ — the coda letter never doubles as a plain onset spelling: ⟨p⟩ the coda only ever appears as the second half of a final-table entry (⟨ap⟩, ⟨aap⟩ …), so there is no onset/coda ambiguity to resolve positionally; the coda is baked into which final-key was written. SYLLABIC NASALS: ⟨m⟩ and ⟨ng⟩ can stand alone as whole syllables (bare nasal nucleus, no vowel) — 唔 'm4' and 吳 'ng4' — written with the same letters as the ⟨m⟩ onset and ⟨ng⟩ onset+coda digraph; this spec keys the syllabic reading as a distinct grapheme ⟨ng̍⟩ (test 3: without a distinct key, the plain ⟨ng⟩ onset/coda entry would win the maximal-munch tokenization of a standalone syllable and misparse it as an onset with no vowel) but cannot likewise disambiguate bare ⟨m⟩ from the ⟨m⟩ onset without a genuine syllable-nucleus predicate this engine does not yet expose for consonant letters (AGENTS.md §1) — a documented gap, not something to enumerate around; bare ⟨m⟩ therefore currently reads through the plain onset mapping. TONE — SCHEMA LIMITATION, same honest treatment as `nan-Latn-poj`: Jyutping marks each syllable's citation tone with a trailing ASCII digit 1-6 (tones 1-6; the three historical entering-tone categories 7/8/9 are not separately numbered in Jyutping, distinguished only by their obstruent coda per LSHK's design). A digit is not a diacritic riding on a vowel grapheme (unlike POJ's combining accents) — it is a free-standing character with its own tokenizer slot — so this spec does not add digit-suffixed grapheme keys (⟨aa1⟩ … ⟨aa6⟩ for every final) because that is exactly the Cartesian-product pattern AGENTS.md §2 forbids: 6 tones × dozens of finals is a nested loop, not an orthographic unit, and the tone digit contributes no segmental information the final's own IPA is missing. `tone_inventory` records the digit-to-contour correspondence as metadata; appending the correct tone letter to a slot's chosen IPA from a digit that sits AFTER the whole syllable (not on any one grapheme) is the same missing engine capability already flagged on `nan-Latn-poj`, and Cantonese's own pervasive tone sandhi (Matthews & Yip 1994) is out of scope for the same reason tone sandhi is out of scope there.

orthography_standard.name: Jyutping (LSHK Cantonese Romanization Scheme)
orthography_standard.notes: Updated 2018 to add the -a and -oet finals; this spec follows the current (post-2018) scheme.

ancestors.notes: Same ISO 639-3-less / Glottolog language (cant1236, Cantonese); this spec supplies the Jyutping Latin-romanization grapheme map that `yue.json`'s Han-script stub explicitly leaves for a romanization to fill, exactly as `nan-Latn-poj` fills the same gap for `nan`.

location.notes: Glottolog's representative point for Cantonese (cant1236), inherited from the `yue` parent.
